items.q: What unfashionable claim does Dex start from?
items.a: Agents solve problems well but **cannot yet write maintainable code without a human**. The factory swapped "human builds" for an agent: building is **minutes**, reviewing is still **hours/days**. Automating build doubles nothing if trust-building still takes days.

items.q: What broke when HumanLayer tried to stop reading code?
items.a: The **light software factory** (agent review, linters, nobody reads). A desktop bug three frontier models could not fix forced them back into months of unread **slop** under user pressure. Recovery cost is paid at the worst time.

sections.title: Front-load judgment where it is cheap

items.q: Which alignment rung does almost everyone skip?
items.a: **Program design**: file placement, call stack, types/signatures, what tests will look like — **before** the agent cooks. A design session at ~**43K tokens** still has full model intelligence; re-steering after thousands of lines is expensive and biased.

items.q: Why don't 99% SWE-Bench scores license you to stop reading?
items.a: RL scores **tests passing**, never design. Maintainability has **no fast oracle**. Match rigor to stage: pre-PMF, vibe; at 5+ engineers or regulated customers, the ladder is step one. If review is the constraint, adding coding agents is the **token-maxing fallacy**.
